title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, add quant profiles and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token serving costs by applying workload-driven defaults for batching and KV-caching while making it safe and reversible for customers. Provide first-class quantization profiles to standardize 4-bit/8-bit variants across model families and add a lightweight unit-economics (unit-econ) toolkit in the Console/CLI so SREs and platform teams can quickly estimate savings. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) autotune engine for batching/caching defaults that samples traffic and recommends conservative defaults (and a rollback path); 2) canonical quantization profiles for GPT-family and Llama-family models plus a validation harness; 3) unit-econ tooling and Console widgets to visualize cost/latency tradeoffs. What changed (high level): - runtime/autotune: implement sampling-based estimator, safe default heuristics, and per-tenant suggestion pipeline. Defaults are non-breaking and gated behind the "autotune_defaults" feature flag. - runtime/batching: expose new DefaultBatchPolicy and integrate with the estimator so we can apply conservative window/size defaults per-model-family. - runtime/caching: add prefix/KV cache hit-rate estimation and recommended TTLs; expose toggles to enable prefix caching by default for chat workloads. - models/quant: add standardized profiles (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) and mapping rules for common families; include conversion scripts and validation tests. - console/unit_econ: CLI tool and Console dashboard panels showing per-model/unit savings, break-even horizon, and projected monthly savings given commit patterns. - docs: runbook for SREs, user docs for how recommendations are surfaced and how to opt-out. Testing and benchmarks: included A/B canary against controlled traffic (benchmarks in perf-canary) showing median per-token cost reduction of ~18% for chat-heavy workloads and negligible latency regression in 95p (<5ms). Rollout plan: feature flag rollout with canary tenants, automatic suggestions sent to tenant admins, and a 7-day automatic rollback if error/latency/regression thresholds are exceeded. Backwards compatibility: changes are opt-in behind feature flags and defaults are conservative; rolling back is a single flag flip. Notes: kept the autotune estimator lightweight to avoid runtime overhead; quant profiles are stored as YAML to make them consumable by both the runtime and external conversion tools.

release_notes:
- Autotune defaults: sampling-based estimator suggests conservative batching and caching defaults per tenant (feature-flagged).
- Quantization: add canonical q4/q8 profiles and conversion/validation tooling.
- Unit-econ tooling: Console dashboard + CLI to estimate per-model and per-tenant savings and break-even windows.
- Rollout: feature flag + canary with automatic rollback on regressions.
